COMMUNITY HELPERS WORKSHEET ACTIVITY · CLASS 33 · AGES 4–5

Librarian — solve it right on the sheet.

Trace LIBRARIAN, match the librarian to the books, the library card and the bookshelf, circle the things you can find in a library, count the books and draw your favorite book.

THE WORKSHEET — WRITE AND DRAW RIGHT ON IT

Your sheet is ready.

Pick a color or the eraser, then trace, match, circle, count and draw straight on the sheet with your finger, a stylus or the mouse. Press Save my work when you are proud — that is what marks this activity cleared for your child.

← TeacherPrevious activityFarmer →Next activity
HOW TO DO IT

Five little steps.

  1. 1

    Trace

    Trace the dotted word LIBRARIAN letter by letter — nine letters, take them one at a time.

  2. 2

    Match

    Draw a line from the librarian to the books, the library card and the bookshelf.

  3. 3

    Circle

    Six pictures sit in the grid — circle every one you could really find in a library. Look closely: would ALL of them be there?

  4. 4

    Count

    Count the books in the count row, then write the number in the box.

  5. 5

    Draw

    Draw your favorite book in the big box — its cover, a character from inside, or the part you love best.

Ask a grown-up to read the steps aloud the first time. After that, you know just what to do.

YOUR PENCIL CASE

Pick your tools.

Pencil, nine crayons, an eraser, undo, redo and clear — the tools appear right here and work on the sheet. Save keeps your finished work as a picture, and your saved work comes back next time.

FOR GROWN-UPS

What this worksheet teaches.

What the child is learning: Who librarians are and what a library holds — books, cards, shelves and computers — plus which everyday objects really belong there and how to write the word LIBRARIAN.

Knowledge to have ready: A librarian helps people find and borrow books: the library card takes books home for a while, the bookshelf keeps every story tidy, and each book comes back so a friend can enjoy it next. Libraries are quiet, friendly places full of stories.

Why this activity matters: A child who knows how the library works owns it for life. Naming the librarian’s tools turns a first visit from overwhelming to exciting, and the find-it-in-a-library grid builds the careful sorting that later sorts letters, numbers and bugs.

  • Community helper vocabulary
  • Tool matching
  • Place-based sorting
  • Word tracing
  • Counting practice
  • Favorite-book drawing

What to say before you start: "This is a librarian — she helps people find wonderful books. Trace her name, then connect the books, the library card and the bookshelf. Now look at the six pictures: which ones could you find in a library? Count the books slowly with your finger, and finish by drawing the book YOU love."

What to look for on the sheet: In the match row, ask which of the three things you hold, which you tuck in a pocket and which stands tall against the wall. In the grid, ask your child to tell a tiny story about each circled picture — librarians love stories. In the draw box, ask for the book’s title out loud before the pencil starts.

Questions to ask along the way: "What does a librarian do all day?" "Which grid pictures could you find at the library?" "What do we do with a book when we finish it?" "What is YOUR favorite book, and who reads it with you?"

Helpful hints without giving it away: Three tiles are worth a family debate: the apple and the scissors live in kitchens and desks, the globe might stand in a library corner, and one bouncy thing belongs on the grass — ask of each: "would I see this on my library visit?" For the count, touch each book spine once.

Parent tips: Pair the sheet with a real library trip this week — let your child carry the card and hand the books over the desk. Owning the borrowing-and-returning ritual is what quietly makes a reader.

Understanding check: Ask: "Who helps you find books? Name two things you saw at the library. How many books?" The helper, two finds, the count = the sheet landed.

Real-life practice: Visit the library and play find-it: the bookshelf, the computer, the desk — every circled picture spotted in real life. Then borrow one book and let your child check it out all by themselves.

This activity belongs to Class 33 — Community Helpers & Our Neighborhood on the Learning Path. Progress is saved on this device for the child chosen in My Classroom — and only a real save of finished work marks it cleared, never just opening the page.
